item.title: AI零幀起手寫運算元，反超DeepSeek人類手寫巔峰：快了9.8%！
item.abstract: AI零幀起手寫運算元，反超DeepSeek人類手寫巔峰：快了9.8%！ 十三 2026-10-30 19:05:06 來源： 量子位 之前還連登昇騰三榜第一 金磊 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 沒有原始碼，沒有論文，直接從零開始。 就在今早，ForgeKernel， 一個無人參與的Agent 在無需參考DeepSeek原始實現的情況下，就當著全網的面，把 DeepSeek最新 的 核心運算元 寫快了 9.8% ！ 並且整個過程的直播，僅僅花了 22.5小時 的時間（從設計算子的角度來看，消耗時間算短的），也引來了不少網友的圍觀： 具體來說，這個直播的內容是一個Agent在輝達B200上，超越DeepSeek-V4.1的 FlashMLA Prefill運算元 。 FlashMLA是DeepSeek開源的注意力核心運算元庫，10月20日剛開源的推理框架DeepInfer也把它整合在內；它出自業內公認Infra最強的團隊之手，可以說是代表了 人類手寫運算元的巔峰 。 而也正如我們剛才所說，AI拿到的只有運算元的數學定義和目標硬體約束，它要 0幀起手 ，通過自進化一輪輪改進。 在這22.5個小時裡，每一次改寫、每一個性能數字的跳動，就這麼水靈靈地擺在了全網觀眾眼前： 第一版通過了正確性檢查，但耗時1834微秒，效率相對較低； 不到4小時，耗時壓到593微秒，降幅約67.6%，已從零逼近當前最佳實現的九成； 第7小時前後，一次核心結構突破讓它先超過了自己的上一代版本，隨後首次超過FlashMLA； 上午9點多，直播結束。最終版本耗時472微秒，FlashMLA為518微秒，快了9.8%。 全程 42 輪迭代，留下 32 個版本，用了1張B200和22個GPU小時；而人類為這個運算元寫的程式碼是， 0行 。 手寫巔峰，就這樣被一份人類沒寫一行程式碼的運算元越過了。 那麼這到底是何許Agent？ 它，正是來自 面壁智慧 的運算元生成系統 ForgeKernel ；並且在本場直播結束之後，智慧進化實驗室隨即聯合OpenBMB社群宣佈 開源 。 不過這場直播還並非是ForgeKernel的首次亮相，早在前幾天，它就已經famous過一次了。 包攬了國產算力三個第一 就在10月27日， 昇騰CANN 官方發文，就“點名”了一下ForgeKernel—— 同時登頂CANNBench 950DT 、 950PR 、 A3 三大硬體榜單！ 這三個榜單分別對應的三類昇騰硬體，它們的成績看點可以說是各有不同。 我們先來看下 950DT 這個榜單，這也是三張榜裡經濟賬算得最明顯的一張。 ForgeKernel在這張榜上以4010.75分排名第一，領先第二名27.8%；基準加速比1.533×，約為第二名的143%。 這就意味著在同等硬體投入下，可用算力增長接近50%，企業的算力採購與部署成本可相應降低約一半。 之所以這個榜單值得關注，是因為950DT是新一代晶片，配套運算元庫尚在建設初期，人工適配週期長，而ForgeKernel率先完成了適配並登頂。 這說明新硬體剛上市，AI就能快速產出高質量運算元，晶片從上市到適配好之間的空窗期，正在被大幅壓縮。 950PR 則是三張榜裡競爭最激烈的一張，前三名的基準加速比都達到了1.3倍： ForgeKernel在這張榜上總分4165.94，同樣排名第一；基準加速比1.638×，約為第二名的1.18倍。 最後，就是 A3 ，也就是目前廣泛使用的昇騰910C。 早在10月15日封榜的CANNBench v1.1中，它就已拿下A3硬體榜第一；v2.0開榜後，這個位置一直沒有讓出，目前總分4341.16，基準加速比1.898×，約為第二名的1.22倍。 在這次直播中，ForgeKernel是跑在輝達B200上，用的是CUDA，這套生態攢了多年的專家經驗；而這三張榜單是在昇騰上跑的，昇騰有自己獨立的架構和工具鏈。 雖然兩邊的軟硬體差別很大，但ForgeKernel卻能用同一套系統，在兩邊都拿到了第一。 那麼接下來的問題是，它是如何做到的呢？ 是無師自通的那種 模型最終能跑多快，很大程度上得看運算元。 因為同一款模型、同一塊晶片，換一套更高效的運算元，效能就會拉開明顯差距。 而長期以來，高效能運算元依賴資深工程師逐個手寫調優，週期長、門檻高。CUDA生態走到今天，靠的是多年的專家積累；而國產晶片每出一代新硬體、每來一個新模型，都要重新適配一遍。 一言以蔽之，人類專家的數量，跟不上晶片和模型的迭代速度。 那麼此局又該如何破解？ 10月27日，ForgeKernel團隊與清華大學等機構在arXiv釋出了一篇名為JustGoal：With Only a Goal，the AI Baseline Is Above the Expert Kernels的論文。 在這篇論文中，研究團隊只給模型一個最佳化目標，不提供任何運算元知識，也不規定固定流程，讓它自己去寫。結果在B200上，模型在10個運算元中的8個跑贏了人類維護的開源庫。 他們還讓同一個模型套上MIT韓松團隊參與開發的專用框架KDA-0.5，在單配置最佳化任務上的平均成績反而只有JustGoal的0.95×。也就是說，寫運算元越來越依賴模型自身的能力，專家預先寫好的經驗和流程，作用在變小。 不過，只給目標也有做不到的地方。模型擅長調細節，卻難以獨立設計好整體架構，常常在開局幾次嘗試中就把路線定死，之後只能在原有架構裡微調。ForgeKernel就是在JustGoal的基礎上，專門補這塊短板的。 它的做法可以分成三部分： 一是把架構設計和實現能力分離，並把架構設計抽象成里程碑，拆解問題； 二是把每一條實測驗證過的硬體經驗存進知識庫，換一個運算元也能接著用； 三是把自己寫出的最好版本當作下一輪的對手，一輪輪自進化。 而這三部分，剛好可以與我們剛才展示的直播一一對應。 ForgeKernel先超過了自己的上一代版本，接著才超過FlashMLA，這就是自進化。 到了後期，它還自己發現Q的突發載入在和KV資料搬運爭搶訪存資源，於是主動控制Q的請求節奏，又壓下2.4%的耗時，這種判斷過去要靠資深專家來做。 △ForgeKernel Live 中的 Agent 執行日誌 放到更多運算元上，ForgeKernel在29項對比中有24項打平或超越專家實現，三套領先Agent系統公開的7個最強運算元，也全部打平或超越。 這份收益，還能在不同的國產晶片之間複製，因為ForgeKernel的設計對國產晶片還有一個好處，那就是不依賴於具體的某一款硬體。 具體的運算元實現，要貼著每款晶片的硬體特性來寫，沒法照搬；但ForgeKernel組織最佳化的方法是通用的，沒有為任何一款晶片預設固定流程。從輝達換到昇騰，它只需把效能分析工具從NCU換成msprof，新晶片需要的硬體知識，再由模型在這塊晶片上邊測邊積累。 這樣一來，ForgeKernel可以快速遷移到其他國產晶片上，新一代國產晶片推出時，也不必再從零搭建一套適配流程。 省下的是真金白銀 如果運算元能快上1%，這又到底意味著什麼呢？ 據Gartner最新預測，2026年全球AI基礎設施支出約1.48萬億美元。按這個量級，算力效率每提升1%，對應的就是約 148億美元 。 若是放到國產晶片上，這筆賬會更加明顯一些。 輝達的CUDA已經被專家優化了多年，現成的高效能運算元很多，AI再往上提速的餘地有限；國產晶片配套的運算元庫還不完善，不少運算元沒有經過充分調優，AI能帶來的提升也就更明顯一些。 ForgeKernel團隊用AI最佳化訓練框架時，也看到了這個差別，同樣的做法在國產晶片上能提速20%～30%，在輝達上為5%～10%，這意味著，ForgeKernel可以進一步提高國產晶片在訓練和推理任務上的價效比，縮小與輝達的差距。 當寫程式碼對AI幾乎不花成本以後，很多以前嫌專家太貴、算不過賬的最佳化就值得做了，比如給某個模型或某顆晶片單獨定製一套運算元。 事實上，這些超越人類專家的運算元並沒有停留在榜單上，而是已經走向了真實的產業一線。 目前，ForgeKernel生成的運算元已正式接入訓練框架，在國產晶片與輝達平臺上完成了MiniCPM5-1B的長訓測試。 更值得注意的是，在這場算力底層的重構中，以DeepSeek V4.1為代表的國產大模型，已經開始參與到運算元的生成和最佳化中；而這些運算元，最終又穩穩地跑在國產晶片之上。 “國產模型寫運算元，國產晶片跑運算元”，一條屬於中國AI的全棧生態閉環正在成型。 這不僅是運算元的勝利，更是RSI（遞迴自進化）落地的真實縮影： AI研發的行為主體，正在從人類轉向AI。 正如面壁智慧智慧進化首席科學家 李宇軒 所說，由於程式碼能被機器快速驗證，工程落地會比理論研究率先實現閉環： 過去，像 FlashAttention 系列這樣需要深度重構架構的頂尖運算元，人類專家往往需要數月甚至半年才能完成一次迭代；而如今在團隊內部，AI 超越最佳人類實現的運算元最佳化任務，最多隻需兩天就能完成。 而隨著ForgeKernel的正式開源，這套方法也將作為基礎設施，為國產晶片廠商和模型團隊提供了新的效率路徑。 以前國產晶片要追趕輝達，難的往往不是硬體指標，反倒是CUDA生態裡堆積了十幾年的專家經驗與軟體分層。但在RSI的範式下，AI正在把這種依靠人力堆疊、耗時數年建立的生態壁壘徹底打穿，直接端到端生成最優解。 當 “國產模型寫運算元，國產晶片跑運算元” 成為新的運算元工程範式，研發的主體或許正在不可逆地從人類轉向模型。但這並不意味著人類專家的離場，只是他們的工作重心發生了根本性的躍遷： 從親手打磨每一行底層程式碼，轉向為AI搭建環境、設定目標與驗證標準，去配合AI把運算元寫得更好。 當人類從程式碼工匠轉變為系統架構師，國產晶片在“能跑”和“跑好”之間的鴻溝，正在被AI以小時為單位迅速填平。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 Deepseek ForgeKernel 運算元 面壁智慧 十三 成立3個月便反超GPT-6 Astra！深圳黑馬首次亮相 item.title: 剛剛，DeepSeek重磅開源：Agent底座架構！
item.abstract: 剛剛，DeepSeek重磅開源：Agent底座架構！ 夢瑤 2026-10-31 21:49:44 來源： 量子位 AI已經自己找到Bug並提交PR 夢瑤 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI DeepSeek，又有新動作了！ 而且這回，官方直接把 Personal Agent 的底層架構思路公開了。 要知道，此前不少人還在等DeepSeek推出傳聞中的「dsh dot」，結果這次先等來了一篇面向工程實踐的架構思路探討—— Super-agent：邁向更自主的Agent系統。 何意味？AI可以在沒人@、沒人下指令的情況下，自己發現Bug、定位問題，甚至主動提交修復PR了。 甚至它還能持續關注工作群訊息，跨平臺協作、並行處理多個複雜任務，甚至實現24小時線上執行。 DeepSeek團隊還曬出了初步實測成績—— 在模擬多工環境中，Super-agent的任務完成時間中位數為12.4分鐘，95分位數為15.7分鐘，表現優於測試中的傳統單會話方案。 AI，真的開始有能力從等待人類逐項分配任務，進一步走向主動發現問題、持續推進工作了。 群裡沒人@，AI已經自己找到Bug並提交PR 在日常軟體開發過程中，開發人員經常碰到的一個問題是，我們需要在不同平臺之間來回切換！！ 比如，先在IM群聊裡討論技術方案，隨後到GitHub提交程式碼，再根據PR評論修改實現。 對於傳統Coding Agent來說，這些操作往往分散在不同會話裡—— 使用者得自己記住每個會話進行到了哪裡，再把相關上下文交代給AI。 DeepSeek團隊在文章中提到，根據他們的觀察，一個人通常只能同時跟進3到5個活躍Session。 這就帶來了一個問題：隨著模型處理單項任務的能力越來越強，多工協作的效率，卻越來越容易受到人類注意力的限制。 好巧不巧的是，Super-agent要解決的，正是這一問題。 在DeepSeek團隊內部執行的例項中，同一個開發任務可以從IM群聊一直延續到GitHub PR評審。 比如，使用者先在群裡決定採用方案A，隨後又在GitHub評論裡要求改成方案B。 Super-agent能夠理解這兩條訊息屬於同一項工作，並據此調整後續執行方向。 使用者面對的始終是同一個Agent，底層的多個會話則由系統自行管理，而且它開始主動參與工作。 這裡還用到了一項技術—— 投機執行（Speculative Execution） 。 就是AI發現某件事可能需要處理時，可以提前在後臺嘗試。 比如群裡有人討論一個Bug，Super-agent便先著手復現、查詢原因，如果最終找到簡單可行的修復方案，就把結果交給使用者。 如果沒有找到有效結果，則可以保持安靜，避免打擾，同樣的思路也能用於個人助手。 收到會議邀約後，AI可以提前檢查日程衝突、整理相關資料，並準備好回覆草稿，等待使用者確認。 這也對應著DeepSeek為Super-agent提出的四個核心特徵： 連續： 跨會話、跨工作平臺保持任務上下文，不用反覆解釋前情。 高效： 多個複雜任務並行執行，耗時任務不會阻塞新的互動。 主動： 持續觀察環境變化，在有必要時自行採取行動。 持久： 長期線上執行，遇到異常能夠嘗試自動恢復。 DeepSeek為此設計了一套雙層架構。 上層叫Router，可以理解為負責接收訊息和統籌任務的排程員，下層叫Worker，則是一組負責具體執行任務的Agent會話。 具體來說，上層的Router相當於總排程員，負責接收訊息、分配任務和維護全域性上下文。 下層的Worker則負責具體執行，多個任務可以同時推進，互不干擾。 值得注意的是，DeepSeek還專門設計了訂閱與直通機制—— 舉個例子，某個Worker接手一條GitHub PR後，就能直接訂閱後續評論。 之後有人提出修改意見，訊息會直接交給這個Worker處理，無需再經過Router層層轉發。 這樣一來，老任務有人持續跟進，新任務也能及時分配，整個系統就能更高效地運轉起來。 24小時線上、自主恢復，實測任務完成時間更穩定 除了多工協作，要讓Super-agent長期自主執行，還得解決訊息過濾、任務阻塞和異常恢復等問題。 先說訊息過濾。 當Agent同時接入工作群、GitHub、郵件等平臺，大量訊息會持續湧入，但真正需要處理的可能只有少數。 為此，DeepSeek設計了兩級事件過濾機制—— 先通過程式規則篩除無關訊息，再由大模型判斷剩餘事件是否需要採取行動，減少不必要的Token消耗。 與此同時，Super-agent還引入了非同步ReAct Loop。 AI執行耗時任務時，仍能繼續響應新指令，無需等上一項任務完成。該機制已在DeepSeek Harness中實現，但尚未預設開啟。 至於24小時線上，DeepSeek採用了計算、狀態與執行環境分離的思路。 Agent的計算邏輯可以在雲端執行，會話狀態獨立儲存，本地裝置則保留原有工作環境，即便電腦暫時離線，雲端Agent也能維持任務狀態，等裝置重新上線後繼續執行相關工作。 更進一步，團隊還引入了獨立的Watchdog（看門狗）機制。 它相當於一個專門負責監督其他Agent的AI，既能檢測程式故障，也能判斷任務是否陷入無效迴圈、偏離目標，並嘗試介入修復。 DeepSeek團隊還進行了一組初步實驗—— 他們模擬了包含約300條訊息、20項工作請求的協作環境，對比Super-agent與傳統單Session加Subagent方案，每種配置重複測試5次。 結果顯示，Super-agent任務完成時間中位數：12.4分鐘，95分位任務完成時間：15.7分鐘。 傳統單Session方案在中性提示下，95分位任務完成時間達到29.5分鐘。 當然，效率提升也伴隨著一定的Token開銷。 item.title: Meet Factory Droid 1.0: A Model-Independent Coding Agent Harness Built on Script Mode
item.abstract: Factory has released Droid 1.0 , the largest update yet to the Factory Droid agent harness. The main change is programmatic tool calling, now on by default. The model writes a program that runs its tools. One model request can now drive hundreds of tool calls. Droid 1.0 is a model-independent coding agent harness from Factory. Factory defines a harness as everything around the model. That means the prompts, the tools, how tool results return, and the loop . Users pick a model or let Factory Router choose a cost-efficient mix. In a standard loop, every tool output lands in the model’s context. With programmatic tool calling (PTC), the model writes a program instead. Droid implements this as a Script tool . The model writes JavaScript that runs in a sandbox. The sandbox has no file, network, or system access of its own. Raw files, search results, and logs stay inside the program. Only printed output returns to the model. Independent calls run concurrently. The idea builds on CodeAct (Wang et al., 2024) . Factory reports these results from its own sessions: On Claude Opus 5.5, Script mode cuts Droid’s cost by 15% versus direct tool calling. It is on by default for 10 models, including GPT-6.1 Sol and Kimi K3. Factory ran each harness against Droid on the same model. Each harness ran 3 trials per task, from October 23 to 28, 2026. Only tasks both harnesses passed in all 3 trials count toward cost and time. Most changes came from an internal Agent Factory loop. Agents read failures and propose changes, tested on every affected model family. Engineers review and merge. *Terminal-Bench 4 figures are Factory’s own runs, from its methodology section . Droid 1.0 ships as a desktop app and terminal UI . The Droid SDK runs the same harness from Node, with sessions, streaming and MCP tools. Paid plans start at $20 per month . item.title: Vercel Labs Open-Sources agent-desktop for Agent Computer Use
item.abstract: Vercel Labs has released agent-desktop , an open-source CLI for AI agent computer use on macOS, Windows and Linux. agent-desktop reads each app through the operating system’s accessibility tree, not through screenshots. An agent gets a JSON snapshot with a ref for every element it can act on. Version 1.0.2 shipped on October 30, 2026, under Apache-2.0. For developers, any shell-capable coding agent can now drive native apps without a vision model. agent-desktop is a Rust CLI and C library from Vercel Labs for reading and operating desktop apps. It is a tool that agents call, not an agent . It embeds no LLM and has no GUI. Every command prints one JSON envelope and exits. The observe, act and verify loop stays in your agent. Each command flows through a fixed chain. The CLI or C library calls agent-desktop-core , which reaches the OS only through a PlatformAdapter trait. One platform crate then talks to the native accessibility API: Core never imports a platform crate. Each binary is compiled to drive exactly one OS. A snapshot assigns qualified refs such as @s8f3k2p9:e8 . The snapshot ID inside the ref makes it self-describing. A bare @e8 is rejected with INVALID_ARGS . When the UI changes, an action returns STALE_REF or AMBIGUOUS_TARGET . The agent then takes a fresh snapshot. Every error carries a disposition . Agents should retry only when it says safe . Ref resolution is strict and fails closed rather than guessing. Dense apps can expose thousands of accessibility nodes. A --skeleton snapshot reads only 3 levels deep . Cut containers report a children_count and get a drill ref. snapshot --root then reads one region into the same snapshot. The builder reported a 78% to 96% token cut versus full-tree dumps in Slack, VS Code and Notion. In Apple Maps, he reported 3,811 tokens per look falling to 273 . A simulated 52-step task dropped from 198k to 31k tokens. These are self-reported figures, not an independent benchmark. Ref actions go through the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus . That is what lets agents work while you keep using the machine. The global --headed flag allows physical input when needed. Every ref action also auto-waits up to 5,000 ms for a visible, enabled, stable target. Model-side computer use tools work from screenshots and pixel coordinates. Anthropic’s docs say each screenshot costs roughly 1,000 to 1,800 input tokens . Its toolset definition adds about 4,500 input tokens per request. OpenAI’s tool similarly returns click, type and scroll actions your code executes. agent-desktop is model-agnostic and returns structure, not images. Microsoft’s UFO² also uses UI Automation, but ships as a full Windows agent. Install with npm install -g agent-desktop . Bun, Yarn and pnpm work too. The package bundles native binaries for x64 and ARM64. Agents learn the tool from bundled docs via agent-desktop skills get desktop . A skill is also listed on skills.sh . The C library lets Python, Swift, Go, Ruby and Node hosts call it in process. For Electron web contents, launch --cdp opens a DevTools port for agent-browser . item.title: Preview web apps live as your coding agent builds them with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
item.abstract: Coding agents now build working web apps: a dashboard, a product page, a prototype that a product team wants to try. The fastest way to review that work is to open the app, use it, ask for a change, and check the result. That loop works well when the app keeps running where the agent edits it, so each change shows up in the browser within seconds. When the app must be copied out and deployed somewhere else first, every change waits for a deployment, and the review slows down to that pace. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with your choice of agent framework and foundation model (FM). AgentCore runtime , a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, runs each agent session in its own isolated microVM. With Session endpoints , you can open an app running in that session from your own browser. Session Endpoints give each session an authenticated URL that forwards each request’s HTTP method, path, query string, and body, and WebSocket connections, to the ports you allow. You can watch the page update as the agent saves each file. In this post, you deploy a coding agent that keeps a Vite website running in its session, then open one local page with a chat on the left and the live website on the right. You ask the agent to switch the site to a dark color theme, follow its steps as they stream in, and watch the website change without a refresh. Finally, you look at what happens internally: a second port in the same session, and the requests the Session endpoint refuses. The complete sample, including the notebook this post follows, is in the 14-remote-access folder of the agentcore-samples GitHub repo . Each session gets its own Session endpoint, and six details shape how you use it. You choose which ports it reaches. You set allowedPorts when you call CreateAgentRuntime : 1–5 entries, each a single port or a range within 8000–12000, excluding the reserved platform ports . Allowing a port doesn’t start a server, so your application must listen on it, bound to 0.0.0.0 . The URL arrives with the session. The InvokeAgentRuntime response carries it in the X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Endpoint-Url header, which SDKs that model it expose as sessionEndpointUrl . Every request is authenticated. For a runtime that uses AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) , each HTTP request, HTTP/2 stream, and WebSocket handshake carries a Signature Version 4 (SigV4) signature. The caller also needs bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeProxy on the runtime and its runtime endpoint. For a runtime with an inbound JSON Web Token (JWT) authorizer , each request carries a bearer token instead. Knowing the URL doesn’t grant access. The host name selects the port. Your client connects on port 443 regardless of the target port, and a prefix on the host name chooses the port inside the session: It carries the protocols your server speaks. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests, including server-sent events and gRPC, and WebSocket connections all pass through. This walkthrough uses HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket. It’s scoped to one session. The URL needs credentials on every request and lasts only as long as the session, so use it to build, test, and review what your agent produces. To serve an app to your users, deploy it to a hosting service such as AWS Amplify Hosting . A browser can’t add a SigV4 signature or a bearer token to the requests a page makes on its own, so the Session endpoint client in the bedrock-agentcore SDK can open a local endpoint on your machine. Your browser opens http://localhost:8088 , and the local endpoint adds your credentials to each request and WebSocket handshake before forwarding it. A Session endpoint is different from a runtime endpoint , which AgentCore runtime already provides. Use a runtime endpoint, such as DEFAULT , to reach your agent, which controls which version of it callers will reach. InvokeAgentRuntime calls resolve through it, so you can keep development and production on different versions and promote or roll back without changing callers. Use a Session endpoint to see what your agent runs in its session, such as a web preview. It’s an authenticated URL that reaches only the ports you allow, works with whichever version the session runs, and stops working when the session ends. For complete documentation, refer to Connect to runtime sessions through a session endpoint . The sample has four parts. A coding agent runs in the session on port 8080 and edits the website’s files with four tools: list, read, write, and edit. The agent starts a Vite development server on port 8090, which serves the website and pushes each saved change to the browser over its hot-reload WebSocket. On your machine, PreviewApp serves the preview page, sends your prompts to InvokeAgentRuntime , and opens a local endpoint for the website. As Figure 1 shows, the preview page loads the website from the Vite development server on port 8090 through the local endpoint and the Session endpoint, and sends your prompts through InvokeAgentRuntime to the agent on port 8080. The numbers show the order of the steps for one request. Figure 1: Solution architecture Before step 1, PreviewApp has already called InvokeAgentRuntime once to start the session, which starts the agent and the Vite development server. PreviewApp read the Session endpoint URL from that response and opened a local endpoint for port 8090. The numbered steps in Figure 1 then follow one request for a change: Port 8080 isn’t in allowedPorts , because InvokeAgentRuntime reaches the agent without going through the Session endpoint. To follow the walkthrough, you need: The sample deploys the agent as a zip file in Amazon S3 with direct code deployment for Node.js , so you don’t need Docker or an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Session endpoints work with microVM runtimes, not with the Instances compute type, and Session endpoint URLs are reachable over public HTTPS. AWS PrivateLink isn’t supported for inbound connections. First, you deploy the runtime, and the configuration you choose here decides which ports the Session endpoint can reach. The deployment script bundles the agent into one file, adds the website and its dependencies for the runtime’s Linux on Arm64 system, uploads the zip to Amazon S3, and creates the runtime. The following excerpt from deploy.py shows the two settings that matter for this post. protocolConfiguration says where the agent listens for InvokeAgentRuntime , and allowedPorts lists the ports the Session endpoint can reach: 8090 for the website and 8081 for the agent’s status route. Port 8080 isn’t in the list, because InvokeAgentRuntime reaches the agent without it. For the port and path settings, refer to Configure your agent’s serving port and invocation path . The website’s Vite configuration makes the development server reachable from the Session endpoint. It listens on 0.0.0.0 at port 8090 and doesn’t restrict the Host header ( server.allowedHosts is true), because requests arrive under a host name the runtime assigns rather than localhost . The Session endpoint authenticates every request before it reaches the server, so the server doesn’t need its own host check. 1. Clone the sample repo and change to the sample folder: 2. Open session_endpoints_preview.ipynb from the sample folder. 3. Run the install cell, which installs the Python dependencies. 4. Run the %run deploy.py cell. Deployment takes a few minutes, mostly waiting for the runtime to reach the READY status. With the runtime ready, you start the preview. One call does three things: it starts a session (which starts the website), opens a local endpoint for port 8090, and serves the preview page on localhost:8087 . Inside start() , the calls that use Session endpoints are short.

item.title: Prospero: A new coding harness for a more civilized age
item.abstract:
Prospero: a new coding harness for a more civilized age October 31, 2026 nullprogram.com/blog/2026/10/31/ I’ve been fascinated with local LLMs for a couple of years now.
The better open weight models, including some that inference on regular,
higher-end consumer hardware at tolerable speeds, are now reliable enough
to handle simpler programming tasks. This requires a coding harness, but
so far this year I’ve been disappointed by all the harness offerings. For
inexplicable reasons most are built with web stacks, and consume enormous
amounts of memory. At its core a coding harness is essentially curl glued
to popen() . This should not require gigabytes of RAM. So I built my own: Prospero . It’s written in my C++ style with a snappy Dear
ImGui docking interface . It uses around two orders of magnitude
fewer resources than other harnesses without sacrificing features. Dark mode aficionados are covered, too: Note that Prospero comes with no model providers built-in. You’re expected
to supply that yourself, such as with llama.cpp , a workplace on-prem
model, OpenRouter, Anthropic API, OpenAI API, etc. (You can’t use your
Claude subscription.) For those unfamiliar with coding harnesses: In a chat interface you and
the AI take turns writing messages to each other. A coding harness extends
this concept, allowing an AI to “talk” to tools offered by the harness.
Tools “reply” with their outputs. A tool might read or write a file, or
run a shell command. An AI will go from tool call to tool call on its own,
looping on the results. Such an AI is called an agent . Occasionally the
AI will send you a message to inform you of progress or to ask a question,
and the chat interface is still there. Some harnesses, including Prospero, allow agents to spawn subagents to
do their bidding, to work in parallel or keep their context clean. That
is, to not fill their working memory with subtasks. Agents can message one
another and coordinate on tasks. Given SSH access to another machine, or
over plain WSL, Prospero can deploy a headless copy of itself to other
hosts so that agents can operate on those systems. The Professional
Edition embeds engines for combinations of x86/x86-64 and ARM64 on
macOS, Windows, and Linux. The Windows x86 engine even works on Windows
XP, and can play solitaire and minesweeper if you ask. The last is because Prospero is one of the few harnesses with desktop
control capabilities. If your model supports vision — any any model worth
using does — then it can “see” your desktop and interact with it. It can
click, type, and drag to test and debug GUI applications live without a
specialized, per-app MCP assist . This headless engine is why no TUI is necessary. The harness engine runs
on the headless system, and the UI runs on your desktop or laptop. With a
little extra setup, the harness to run fully independently of the GUI, so
that it will continue without the GUI system attached — re-attachable
later. Because Prospero is so lean, it may be the only harness that can drive a fuzz campaign , particularly on a headless system, without the
Linux OOM killer targeting the memory-gobbling harness rather than the
out-of-control fuzz target that triggered it. So many times I’ve checked
back in on a fuzz campaign hours later, to find nothing was accomplished
because the harness process is gone. (Why have an agent run a fuzz campaign? Because it can fix discovered bugs
on the fly and keep the campaign going! It’s a no brainer.) Configuration The configuration lives at ~/.config/prospero/prospero.ini . Easy to
edit. No JSON, thank goodness. Check it into source control, copy-paste
it. All the usual benefits. Alternatively, the Settings page can reach
every setting from the GUI, so you don’t have to edit the INI by hand. INI
files can also include each other, not just naming file system paths but
URLs: include = https://example.com/prospero.ini The idea is to allow a live shared or managed configuration. Includes by
URL are restricted in what they can set, with a hard rule against anything
which might appear in shell command. Some trust is still required, as a
configuration can extract an environment variable by using it as an API
key and supplying an endpoint it controls. Prospero fetches a model list and other parameters like context size from
the endpoint, but you might want to tweak it. A typical configuration may
look like: model = falstaff/Qwen3.8-27B [endpoint falstaff] url = http://falstaff.local/ key = env:FALSTAFF_API_KEY [model Qwen3.8-27B] edit_format = replace template.reasoning_effort = medium [model Qwen3.8-27B-xhigh] like = Qwen3.8-27B template.reasoning_effort = xhigh [web] search = searxng url = https://search.example.com/ key = env:EXAMPLE_API_KEY Passive rendering The ImGui paradigm typically uses active rendering , redrawing on vsync
like a video game. This is appropriate in some contexts, like interfaces
within video games. Less so for mostly-static text-oriented UIs, such as a
coding harness. Instead Prospero uses passive rendering with settle
frames to finish animations before going idle. When there’s nothing to
do, Prospero does nothing. It won’t chew on the GPU while the agent is
waiting on a build. Never wait forever An annoyance with most other harnesses is how easily they get stuck. I set
a long-running task, go to sleep, and in the morning find the harness hung
on a trivial issue two hours into the night, wasting the rest. Therefore
Prospero prime design principle: Never wait forever . Every operation
has a deadline. This decision influences everything. If you’re not there
to grant a requested permission, the agent will get a denial by timeout
and must do without. To assist, Prospero will raise a system toast when an
agent requires your attention so that you’re less likely to miss it if
you’re attending. The harness itself plows through intermittent errors , trying its best to
drive the agent to complete its task. All network requests have timeouts,
and watchdogs prevent endless waiting . Agent mailboxes are
bounded . Shell commands that hit their timeout convert to asynchronous background
commands. The agent can continue to wait on them, with a timeout, and so
will be woken at regular intervals to decide if it should continue. The one exception is Plan mode, where it waits indefinitely after offering
a plan or requesting clarification ( ask_user tool). It’s expected that a
user is attending to the agent during Plan mode. No stray processes The harnesses I’ve used have improved, but another regular annoyance
earlier this year was agents starting processes that never get cleaned up.
An agent kicks off a parallel build, hits a timeout because it was too
optimistic, the build “stops” by killing a piece of the build system. But
actually the build continues anyway , at least in part. The agent tries
again, and now two builds are going, interfering with each other, making a
mess and bringing my system to its knees. For awhile I was wary of letting agents run builds in certain harnesses,
which is a terrible outcome. You want agents to close the loop and
iterate independently. A human in the loop is like putting a ball and
chain on the agent, giving up most of its advantages. Prospero promoting a synchronous timeout to an asynchronous task is a huge
improvement on its own, but there’s an additional principle at play: The
whole process tree lives and dies together. When a command is stopped, it
stops . This is trivial on Windows , though few harnesses seem to
take advantage of it. It’s more difficult on macOS and Linux, but Prospero
follows through. Built-in self-help Like every harness, Prospero supports skills , a pre-packaged set of
instructions on how to accomplish some task (“I know kung fu.”). Prospero
contains a skill on itself and can read its built-in documentation.

(168 points, 111 comments on Hacker News)

物理AI新單位“Worken”，用來衡量機器人的有效智慧工時。 智元還給Worken設計了套績效結算公式： Worken=活躍機器人數量×自主工作時長×產出效能比 活躍機器人數量反映部署規模，自主工作時長看機器人能否在無需人工接管的情況下持續作業，產出效能比則衡量實際產出效率。 Fine，以後矽基人再也不能擱那兒純摸魚了╮(╯▽╰)╭ 不過，智元這次可不光是給機器人安排了績效考核。 圍繞如何讓機器人真正創造價值，智元這次也帶來了從模型、本體到作業系統的一系列技術進展，覆蓋具身智慧的運動、作業和互動等核心能力。 譬如新模型這邊，具身基座模型GO-3 Preview已經拿下三項具身智慧評測榜單第一，互動大模型WITA-OMNI也在四項評測榜單中登頂。 會後訪談時，稚暉君表示“ 萬臺下線，只是製造業的勝利；萬臺上崗，才是物理AI的勝利 ”。 但要讓機器人持續交出這份績效，光有一套計算公式可不夠。 智元這次釋出的新模型、新本體和新系統，正好可以串起Worken背後的技術佈局。 從模型到本體，智元新發布了些啥？ 本次創新日，智元釋出了新一代具身基座模型GO-3 Preview和全模態端到端互動大模型WITA-OMNI。 兩個模型分別瞄準機器人工作的兩類核心能力。 GO-3主要面向作業智慧，幫助機器人理解任務、生成動作並完成操作；WITA-OMNI面向互動智慧，讓機器人能夠理解人、回應人，並在真實環境中通過語音、表情和動作進行自然交流。 與此同時，智元還在推進運動智慧、硬體架構和作業系統的升級。 模型負責提升能力，本體和系統負責承載並協同能力，真實部署則檢驗這些技術能否在工作現場發揮作用。 由此便有了智元互動智慧、運動智慧、作業智慧的“三智”佈局。 作業智慧 item.title: [AINews] Google admits AI Mode hurts Search revenue; -15% $500B drop worst since 2004 IPO. AI Bear Market coming?
item.abstract: As an engineer-focused newsletter we only very rarely let financial stories through (our last example was Jan 2025 ), but when this is about the future of Google and Google Search , with a recently departed AI leadership, you cannot not care. At its heart is the tension between overview pages and underlying pages they summarize. Any good enough summary obviates the need for you reading the source. Google’s Featured Snippets or Knowledge Panels have long had that tension with the publishers that supply that data. But now, Google’s own AI Overviews are potentially affecting traffic with… Google's Search revenue. Google doesn’t break out AI Mode in sufficient detail that we can make any sort of rigorous analysis, but most people are quoting Philipp Schindler (Chief Business Officer): “It’s worth noting that the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode.” Together with other bad earnings results it set off a range of steep declines throughout tech: This is against a backdrop of souring tech/AI sentiment in public markets - and with OpenAI raising at $1.25T not $1.4T , not the sort of thing you want in the lead up to one of the biggest tech IPOs of all time. AI News for 10/29/2026-10/30/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! Claude Ultra Drops the 5-Hour Limit as Anthropic Renames Its Max Tiers Plan rename : Anthropic renamed its Max tiers. Max 5x is now "Max" at $100/month, and Max 20x is now "Ultra" at $200/month. Existing subscribers do not need to take any action ( announcement ). 5-hour limit removed : Verified Ultra accounts no longer have the 5-hour session limit. The change starts today for most existing subscribers ( @claudeai , @bcherny , @alexalbert__ ). Rollout caveat : Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until they are verified, which Anthropic describes as an anti-fraud measure. Affected users will get an email when the limit is lifted. Unchanged : Weekly limits stay the same. Reaction : The change was widely welcomed, with posts such as "Huge!!!" ( @theo ) and "Anthropic is on a run" ( @kimmonismus ). Subscription economics (unverified analysis) : @teortaxesTex cites a SemiAnalysis reconstruction of Anthropic's finances. Margins : Anthropic's API margin is put at about 92%, versus about 84% for DeepSeek. Subsidy : Opus on subscriptions is described as heavily subsidized, breaking even only below about 21.3% utilization. Revenue vs compute : A follow-up estimates that subscriptions bring in about 18% of revenue while using more than 50% of compute ( thread ). Comparison with DeepSeek : The same author argues that a heavily subsidized DeepSeek V4.1-Flash plan ($10 for about $76.5 of API-equivalent usage) is close in price per token to Claude subscriptions ( long post ). Frontier and Open Model Releases Gemini 4 Carbon (Google DeepMind) : The model is ranked #1 in Text Arena, #2 in Agent Arena and #4 in WebDev, and changed the Pareto frontier in all three ( Arena ). Research quality : Perplexity reports a new state of the art on its WANDR long-form research benchmark. Carbon is coming to Pro and Max users inside Computer "once we have sufficient token capacity" ( @AravSrinivas ). Genie 4 world model : Google's new world model generates interactive simulations with sound that users can steer in real time ( @Google ). Availability : It is a research preview for trusted testers. It is coming soon to Google AI Ultra in Project Genie and to Gemini API and AI Studio early-access partners ( rollout ). Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk") : The model has 1T parameters ( TRL ) and 1M-token context ( llama.cpp ). Fine-tuning : Axolotl has day-0 LoRA support. Its recommended recipe uses NVFP4 experts with merge-aware LoRA and fits on one 8xB200 node ( @winglian ). Coding : One third-party coding benchmark ranks it the second-best open-source model ( @ThibaultJaigu ). NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 tech report : Super has 120B total and 12B active parameters and handles text, image and video. It scores 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro, beating Nemotron 3 Ultra with about 4.6x fewer active parameters ( summary ). Lightning variant : A 30B text-only model with 3B active parameters. Serving : Up to 4,856 output tok/s/GPU on GB200 while holding at least 50 tok/s/user. Quantization : NVFP4 recovers 99.62% of median BF16 accuracy. Smaller and specialized models : Microsoft computer-use agent : A 4B hybrid agent that can both click and write code scores 66.0% on OSWorld-Verified, ahead of 27B and 30B agents ( @HuggingPapers ). Phonic-1 : Claims #1 on AA's speech-to-speech index, on τ-Voice and on Sierra's τ³-Voice ( @moinnadeem ). It was built by a 10-person team with $4M ( @davisblalock ). mischief 1 (BioComputing Co) : An image-to-video model priced from 0.5¢ per second. The company says it is at least 5x faster than its base model and draws on biological-neuron research ( launch ). Skepticism : Critics say the link between neuron research and the model is unexplained or marketing ( @willdepue , @jachiam0 ). OpenAI Private Intelligence : An enterprise offering that gives businesses stronger data controls when using OpenAI's top models. It is being built with large customers ( @OpenAI ). Independent Evals, Benchmarks and Quantization Disputes AA Intelligence Index v5 : 60% of the score now comes from private or held-out tests. Scores are Opus 5.5 (max) 58, GPT-6 Astra 57 and GPT-6.1 Sol 55, with Sol costing about one-eighth as much per task ( summary ). Effort scaling : Opus 5.5 scores 35 at low effort versus 58 at max, at about 10x the cost. AA-Omniscience v1.1 : The knowledge and hallucination benchmark was cut from 6,000 to 3,000 questions, with saturated items removed ( details ). Public set : A new 300-question public set correlates 0.99 with private scores. Leaders : Gemini 4 Carbon leads at Net Score 54, followed by Opus 5.5 at 48 and Fable 5.1 at 46. Other results : Gemini 4 Argon has the lowest hallucination rate at 4%. MiniMax M3.1 Flash fell 22 points (16 → −6). Agent Arena cost data : An analysis of 26K sessions finds that without prompt caching, a task on a top-10 agent would cost 3.6x as much ( Arena ). Example : A typical Fable 5.1 task costs $7.44 with caching versus $27 without. Cache expiry : A single cache invalidation adds about 5% to a task's bill. GPT-6.1 Terra (Max) : It entered Agent Arena at #8 with a 10.6% net improvement at $0.62 median cost per task ( Arena ). DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 quants : Unsloth released dynamic v3.1 GGUFs that run on 64GB+ RAM ( @UnslothAI ). Reproducibility dispute : Unsloth says it cannot reproduce GSQ-RCO's numbers. For example, the claimed 100% AIME25 score at 1-bit came out as 91.88% in its runs ( @danielhanchen ). Reasoning length : Unsloth also reports that lower-bit quants reason somewhat longer than the unquantized model. DeepSeek-Cyber (unconfirmed) : Leaked "dreamed" scores circulated, including about 92% on CyberGym and 96.8% on ExploitBench at 3,000 steps. They are not an official release. Third-party data : Per Fireworks, CyberGym pass@3 moved only from 94.82% (0910) to 95.36% (1017). @teortaxesTex argues that near saturation, almost any number is consistent with the same checkpoint. Analyst view : The rumored scores are argued to fit a guardrail-free 1017 rather than a new model ( analysis ). Usage restriction : The model reportedly cannot be used by Chinese entities sanctioned by the US government ( note ). Safety, Security and Agent Supply Chain Automated red-teaming (Anthropic) : Thousands of Claude agents were tasked with evading a training-data monitor ( @AnthropicAI ). Findings : The agents produced data that looked benign, such as wrestler mentoring stories or beekeeping Q&A, but taught misaligned behavior. Use : These examples can be used to improve future monitors.

item.title: Agents Prompt People: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work
item.abstract: At AI Engineer New York this month, we sat down with Aman Singh , the lead AI Engineer at Arca , an “AI-native” company providing wealth management services. We discovered that while agents do most of the background work in the firm, there are guardrails in place to ensure that human advisors are making the final decisions. The goal is for AI to guide the process; or as Singh nicely put it, “agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.” Arca recently raised $48.5 Million in a round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Index Ventures and Venrock. One of the features of using AI in financial services, explained Singh, is that it’s typically long-horizon work — although not long-running. In his AIE presentation, Singh noted that agent tasks at Arca can take up to ten days. “It's very stop-start, there's many actors in between, many decision points, many handoffs,” he said. For this reason, Arca has developed an internal memory system . “So we have this persistence for every client ,” Singh said in our podcast discussion. “What has happened so far? What are we tracking for next? What needs to happen immediately in the next couple of days [and] what are we tracking for the long term? Which individual is responsible for which action? All of this is being tracked by our memory systems that our agents contribute to.” Arca uses models from frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI, with Claude its primary model provider. The company has built its own harness , which automatically selects the best model to use for a particular task, based on the company’s internal benchmarks. Owning the harness, rather than using a managed agent harness, also means that Arca has the flexibility to change model providers if it needs to. Safety is obviously key for financial services. Singh noted that although agents do much of the work, an agent’s role is limited to analysis and proposing solutions. Trading and any other money movement is handled by a human advisor. “All of our safety restrictions are fully deterministic,” he said. “And they take the decision making off the agent's hands.” In other words, there are certain tools and tasks the agent can execute by itself — but not ones that involve risk to the client. Arca also runs verification checks on known AI security issues, such as prompt injections. Arca’s agent isn’t itself sandboxed, but it does use sandboxes for computation. Singh explained they’ve gone even further, with extra security measures for handling sensitive data. “We've built systems to make it safe for code inside of that sandbox to access our data,” he said. “So we have this thing which translates the code it [the agent] wrote into a strict format that we expect, throw away the code, and you install guardrails on that format before it reaches your back end. So we allow the agents to use code to query our data, which means that they can aggregate it, they can munge it, they can work with it as they see fit to produce [things] like a financial plan.” Another interesting process Arca has implemented is using feedback from human advisors, along with traces from the agents, to improve the harness. item.title: Build a Validated Kubernetes Runtime for NVIDIA Dynamo
item.abstract: Teams building AI applications need a repeatable path from a model configuration to a working inference endpoint. NVIDIA Dynamo is a distributed inference framework that coordinates model serving across GPU workers. Deploying it on Kubernetes is only a first step. A successful model deployment requires more: GPU drivers, resource allocation, scheduling, networking, and monitoring must all work together. Resolving these dependencies takes time away from testing model behavior, serving performance, and application integration. The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform brings together technologies to help the ecosystem design, build, and operate more efficient AI factories, and Dynamo is one of them. To make management of those infrastructure dependencies easier, the platform contains NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime (AICR). It packages NVIDIA Dynamo and its supporting infrastructure into validated recipes. Each recipe defines a configuration for a specific environment and workload, including pinned component versions, compatibility constraints, and validation checks. AICR gives platform teams a repeatable way to deploy and check the runtime, providing developers with a consistent foundation for serving models and testing applications. This walkthrough covers the infrastructure that supports Dynamo on Kubernetes, compares two routing options, and shows how to deploy and validate the runtime with AICR. Why the underlying runtime matters for Dynamo Running a model with Dynamo on Kubernetes starts with a DynamoGraphDeployment that specifies how vLLM , SGLang , or NVIDIA TensorRT LLM should run in pods on the cluster. But the graph is only the top of the stack. A production inference cluster also needs a runtime layer below it. It has to answer questions like: Is the NVIDIA GPU Operator installed with a driver stack that matches the nodes? Are GPU nodes labeled and discoverable? Does the cluster expose GPUs through the expected Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver? Can the scheduler place GPU workers with the required topology and gang scheduling semantics? Are node health signals available before workloads land on a degraded node? Is Prometheus reachable for Dynamo and accelerator metrics? Is the Gateway API / Endpoint Picker (EPP) path configured when the deployment should be Kubernetes-native at ingress? AICR captures these runtime requirements in the recipe. What AICR ships for Dynamo An AICR Dynamo recipe packages both Dynamo and the cluster runtime components it depends on. AICR ships version 1.4.2 of the dynamo-platform chart, which includes the Dynamo operator, Dynamo runtime images, and resources such as the nvidia.com/v1beta1 DynamoGraphDeployment CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) . v1beta1 replaces the former v1alpha1 API version. Table 1 lists the supporting infrastructure components included in the recipe. Prerequisite Requirement Component in the AICR recipe GPU driver stack Driver and GPU software stack that matches the nodes NVIDIA GPU Operator GPU discovery GPU nodes labeled and discoverable for placement Node Feature Discovery GPU allocation GPUs exposed through Kubernetes-native Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) DRA Driver for NVIDIA GPUs Scheduling GPU workers placed with the required topology and gang scheduling KAI Scheduler Inference Workload Orchestration Multi-component serving graphs started, placed, and scaled as coordinated groups Grove Node health Health signals available before workloads land on a degraded node NVSentinel and Nodewright , where supported by the selected recipe Metrics Cluster, accelerator, and Dynamo service metrics collected Prometheus stack Ingress Gateway / EPP path configured when ingress is Kubernetes-native agentgateway and Gateway API resources, described in the routing sections Table 1. Runtime prerequisites below Dynamo and the components the AICR recipe installs for each In addition, the recipe pins component versions and records configuration values, node selectors, tolerations, checksums, and validation expectations to make deployment reproducible. With Dynamo 1.4, frontends, workers, optional Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) / Endpoint Picker Plugin (EPP) components , and other Dynamo services discover each other through Kubernetes resources. AICR’s default path therefore no longer uses NATS, and the dynamo-platform chart no longer installs it by default. NATS remains available as an opt-in for deployments that need it. Agentic workloads repeatedly extend long token prefixes, including system prompts, tool definitions, conversation history, and tool results. If a turn reaches a worker without that prefix in GPU memory, the system reprocesses intermediate tokens instead of reusing cached results. Dynamo routes requests to workers that already hold the relevant KV blocks, either through its frontend router or through GAIE/EPP integration at the Gateway API layer. Dynamo can also separate prompt processing (prefill) from token generation (decode), an architecture known as disaggregated serving. On KV-cache misses, all or part of the prompt must be reprocessed by the prefill pool. Decode workers then take over token-by-token generation, which has different GPU, memory, latency, and batching characteristics. The cache miss rate depends on the workload. Long-running agentic sessions behave differently from one-off chat requests. Disaggregated serving enables operators to scale and tune prefill and decode capacity independently for a given request mix. The request plane and KV-cache event plane are separate. In Dynamo 1.4.2, the default AICR Kubernetes path uses TCP for requests and ZMQ for KV-cache events. Each vLLM worker engine emits raw KV-cache events through a local ZMQ publisher, for example, with the following vLLM configuration: --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config \ {"enable_kv_cache_events": true, "publisher": "zmq", "endpoint": "tcp://*:5557"} Dynamo’s worker runtime then subscribes to that local vLLM event source, normalizes the events, and republishes them onto the Dynamo event plane. Both the native Dynamo Frontend router and the GAIE/EPP path use this Dynamo-managed KV-cache state to make routing decisions. What are the Dynamo routing paths on Kubernetes? Dynamo supports two routing paths on Kubernetes. The first uses the Dynamo Frontend router for worker selection. The second uses a Kubernetes Gateway API implementation for ingress and Dynamo EPP for endpoint selection. AICR ships and validates the Dynamo runtime for either topology. Path 1: Dynamo Frontend router The default path exposes a Dynamo Frontend behind a Kubernetes Service. Running with DYN_ROUTER_MODE=kv , the Frontend tokenizes each request, scores eligible workers using prefix overlap and current load, selects a worker, and dispatches the request through the Dynamo request plane, which uses TCP by default. This path is suitable when an application team owns a model-specific endpoint or an existing edge proxy only needs to forward traffic to the Dynamo Frontend Service. It is the smallest topology for deploying and validating a Dynamo graph and is the most production-proven serving option. It does not require the additional gateway and EPP components used in Path 2. Figure 1. The Dynamo Frontend selects a vLLM worker based on KV-cache overlap and load. Requests use the TCP request plane; worker KV-cache events reach the Frontend through the ZMQ-backed event plane Path 2: Gateway API Inference Extension and Dynamo EPP This path integrates Dynamo with the Gateway API and Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE). In the AICR example, agentgateway resolves an HTTPRoute to an InferencePool . The Dynamo operator creates that InferencePool from the DynamoGraphDeployment : its selector identifies eligible worker pods, while its endpointPickerRef identifies the Dynamo EPP Service. The gateway invokes the Dynamo EPP through GAIE’s endpoint-selection interface.

item.title: Malware uses LLMs to rank victims by how much they're worth
item.abstract:
VOLTA is a mature stealer implant with an optional AI-integration layer. After stealing credentials, sessions, and cryptocurrency wallets, VOLTA sends a structured evidence bundle to an LLM to rank the victim’s assets by monetization value. If a model refuses to perform the target assessment, VOLTA fails over to a three-model chain, implying a direct engineering effort and expectation of hitting model guardrails. This stealer is self-deleting, and there is no attacker-owned infrastructure. The novelty in the AI-integration is that it is not supporting a traditional malware capability but working as an intelligence analyst on behalf of the operator. There is a new idea in the cybercrime world — cast a wide net, steal everything, and let AI sort out the specifics. A new malware self-named “VOLTA-AUTODOXER,” surfaced through the CAIRN research effort , is a self-deleting Windows infostealer that augments its post-theft workflow with an LLM-powered victim-profiling stage. After harvesting the standard stealer haul, including browser passwords; cookies; payment cards; cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases; Discord, Telegram, Steam, and Roblox sessions; Microsoft OAuth tokens; SSH and cloud-provider keys; Wi-Fi profiles; and screenshots, VOLTA builds a structured evidence bundle about the person behind the machine. This bundle contains geolocation and home address, employer and employer domain, inferred birth year, card last-4 digits, Slack workspaces, document authorship metadata, iPhone backup indicators, and a live Roblox account valuation. It then uses stolen session access to enrich that bundle further: searching the victim's Gmail for purchase receipts to corroborate a home address, pulling UberEats and DoorDash order history, and enriching Discord accounts via the stolen token. The bundle is serialized and POSTed to OpenRouter under a system prompt that instructs the model to act as "a forensic intelligence analyst drafting a target assessment." The required output includes a section titled “WHAT THEY'RE WORTH” with valuables ranked by monetization with a low/medium/high tier, and a section on “THEIR OPSEC” containing an assessment of the victim's security posture and password hygiene. The model is the operator's triage analyst; it turns a raw credential log into a prioritized and citation-backed dossier of the victim and their monetizable assets. Figure 1. The VOLTA-AUTODOXER workflow. The AI configuration: “Go deep, not wide... Be blunt, specific, accurate.” VOLTA uses a multi-model architecture to fall back resiliently if it hits a model’s refusal, checking each response for phrases like “I can’t” or “I’m not able,” before passing on to a chain of up to three models. Endpoint https[ :]// openrouter [ .]ai/ api /v1/chat/completions Default model anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 Fallback chain moonshotai /kimi-k2 → google/gemini-2.5-flash Temperature 0.2 — deterministic, consistent output Request format Hand-assembled JSON; no SDK; User-Agent Mozilla/5.0 Figure 2. Hardcoded model selection. Figure 3. Failover model selection to kimi-k2, and then gemini-2.5-flash. Model temperate controls the randomness and predictability of LLM-generated text. The low hardcoded temperature value (0.2) suggests the attacker is emphasizing accuracy and consistency. The malware also employs a chain of cascading models in the event of failures. This multi-model architecture suggests that the operator is anticipating encountering refusals, with the fallback pivoting to a few, smaller, and more permissive models. The system prompt directly reveals the operator’s use case: Produce a concise analytical assessment of the victim’s suitability as a target, backed by an auditable trail of citations. Figure 4. VOLTA's raw system prompt. The prompt also asks for something out of the ordinary, but that agents excel at: making connections between sparse and disparate data. For example, encouraging connections like the victim’s names, addresses, or universities to patterns in their passwords. In this case, the model isn't being asked to find data; rather, it’s being asked to stretch the data and make useful inferences that extend the value of what has been scraped. Stealer capabilities VOLTA’s capabilities are directly aligned with the records produced in modern digital life, and well beyond basic credential theft. In a single pass, the stealer can extract browser credentials, cookies, and saved payment cards across Chromium-based browsers. It hits Firefox and Thunderbird, Outlook profiles, Slack workspaces, Steam and Battle.net sessions, Discord tokens, Telegram sessions, Roblox accounts, and SSH and cloud-provider config files (gcloud, OpenVPN, Hide.me). VOLTA doesn’t just copy cryptocurrency wallets, but runs an embedded cracker against the vault inline, writing the result to a WALLET VAULTS CRACKED line in its own report. Every saved Wi-Fi password on the machine is pulled via a direct call to WlanGetProfileList and dumped to plaintext. Figure 5. VOLTA dumps plaintext passwords for every saved Wi-Fi network on the host. Figure 6. The organized collection targets. What really sets VOLTA apart from commodity stealers is what comes after the initial collection. There is a live enrichment pass that leverages stolen sessions to deep dive the victim’s data. For example, using the victim's own authenticated Gmail tokens, it queries their inbox for receipts from Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal, then review those receipts to establish a confirmed home address. Stolen Uber Eats and DoorDash sessions are called directly for order history. The Discord token is re-used to enrich the victim's account profile. Roblox inventory is valued via a live “Rolimons[.]com” lookup. Figure 7. That’s right: Your Uber Eats history is now a potential liability. After the collection and enrichment stages are complete, the data is assembled and structured locally in a file called “Identity_Report.txt”. This file is serialized into a bundle as JSON and POSTed to OpenRouter along with the system prompt. The returned payload is received as “AI_Analysis.txt”. Both files exfil together in “volta_dox.zip”. Figure 8. VOLTA’s exfil can happen in three stages: 1) after the stealer runs (“volta_log.zip”), 2) after the AI call (“volta_dox.zip”), (3) if the network enrichment produces anything (“volta_doxnet.zip”). The inference round-trip happens entirely through the victim's own network connection, on their own machine, before the result is exfiltrated. Deployment model Instead of hardcoding its Telegram channel, API keys, and settings directly into the code (which is likely what someone writing a tool for personal use would do) VOLTA uses a template with six swappable slots, filled in at build time. This suggests it’s a builder model: The author sells access, the customer provides their values, and the builder compiles a custom binary for each order. The credentials in those slots are encrypted, but not in a meaningful way. The key is SHA-256 of two constants sitting in the same binary, but it's presumably there because customers expect their API keys not to be sitting in plaintext, not because it provides real protection. Anyone who reverses the file can recover them. If VOLTA is indeed a commoditized malware, then the AI dossier capability isn't something the author invented for their own operations. It is a feature which enables a customer of any level of sophistication to point it at victims and start receiving ranked target assessments in their Telegram inbox. All the observed endpoints for this malware are third-party controlled. There is no actor-owned infrastructure. Countermeasures Much of the token-stealing capability of VOLTA relies on techniques to bypass App-Bound Encryption (ABE) in Chrome. An application control policy that restricts which processes may launch Chrome with --headless would block the ABE decryption path entirely.

item.title: Managing Amazon Bedrock costs end to end: A playbook for FinOps and platform teams
item.abstract: Cost management for generative AI is a shared responsibility between the teams that build applications and the teams accountable for cloud spend. Many teams start by comparing per-model token rates and asking application teams to shorten prompts. Those steps help, but they don’t answer the questions that finance and engineering leaders ask as usage scales: which team spent this, on which workload, and was that spend inside an approved budget? Agentic workloads make those questions more pressing. A conversational assistant typically issues one model invocation per user turn. An agentic workflow, such as an AI coding assistant that plans a change, reads files, calls tools, and iterates, issues many invocations per task and carries a larger context on each one. Token consumption therefore scales with the degree of autonomy you grant the workflow and the size of the context it carries, rather than with the number of user interactions. Because consumption is a function of how a workload is designed and operated, cost management for generative AI is an architectural and operational discipline. Published averages are a poor substitute for your own numbers: use the AWS Pricing Calculator and the Amazon Bedrock pricing page to model rates, and use Step 2 of this post to measure what your workloads actually consume. The fix isn’t a cheaper model or a smaller prompt. It’s an operating model: a repeatable loop that attributes every dollar to an owner, makes every request observable, alerts on and enforces budgets before overspend compounds, optimizes the platform defaults that drive most waste, and reviews the whole system on a cadence. In this post, you learn how to manage Amazon Bedrock cost in five steps. You attribute every dollar to an owner, make every request observable, control spend with budgets and enforcement, optimize the platform defaults that drive most avoidable spend, and operate a review cadence that turns data into decisions. This approach is built from AWS building blocks, and you can customize it and apply it to your own environment. The post is written for two audiences: FinOps practitioners who own attribution, chargeback, budgets, and anomaly review, and platform engineering teams who own logging, request metadata, enforcement, and routing defaults. Five stages, run as a loop. Attribute: every Amazon Bedrock dollar lands on an identity, team, and application in the billing pipeline. Observe: every request is logged with enough metadata to explain what generated the spend. Enforce: budgets have teeth, with alerts at minimum and hard blocks where the risk demands them. Optimize: the platform defaults (model routing, caching, token limits) remove waste centrally instead of asking every team to be careful. Operate: a small scorecard and a review cadence turn the data into decisions. FinOps leads stages one and five. Platform engineering leads two through four. The review is joint. The stages are sequenced deliberately. Each one depends on the ones before it, and teams that jump straight to optimization without attribution and observability are guessing. Figure 1: The five-stage operating model, run as a continuous loop You can’t manage what you can’t attribute, and everything downstream (chargeback, budgets, enforcement, anomaly detection) depends on this stage. The foundation is the granular cost attribution of Amazon Bedrock (see Introducing granular cost attribution for Amazon Bedrock ): Amazon Bedrock automatically attributes inference costs to the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) principal that made the call, across all models, with no resources to manage. The caller’s ARN lands in the line_item_iam_principal column of the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) 2.0 , and coverage spans IAM users, roles, federated identities, and API keys. This is invoice-grade, per-identity attribution with no custom infrastructure. The pattern that deserves the most attention is the shared-role problem, because it is where most platforms silently lose attribution. A large language model (LLM) gateway that calls Amazon Bedrock through a single IAM role attributes every dollar to that one role, eliminating per-user visibility entirely. The fix is per-user session management. The gateway assumes the Amazon Bedrock invocation role once per user, passing the user’s identity as the role session name and their attributes as session tags, then caches those credentials for up to an hour (one AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) call per user per hour, not per request). This needs two roles: a gateway execution role holding sts:AssumeRole and sts:TagSession permissions, and the Amazon Bedrock invocation role it assumes. The result is line_item_iam_principal entries like assumed-role/BedrockRuntimeRole/gw-alex , each carrying its user’s tags: per-user and per-tenant attribution restored behind a shared gateway. Amazon Bedrock offers two more attribution mechanisms, each suited to a different pattern. Application inference profiles are pre-created, per-application resources on the bedrock-runtime endpoint that carry cost allocation tags. You create one profile per application per model per AWS Region, and callers reference the profile ARN, which fits teams with a small and stable set of applications and models. Projects and workspaces serve the bedrock-mantle endpoint (Responses API, Chat Completions API). A project isn’t tied to a specific model, so a single project ID spans many models, which fits teams whose model usage changes frequently. You pass the project ID at client initialization, and its tags flow to CUR 2.0 and Cost Explorer (see Manage AI costs with Amazon Bedrock Projects ). Projects are the attribution path for OpenAI-compatible workloads on Amazon Bedrock. For bedrock-runtime workloads, we recommend IAM principal attribution through session tags as the primary mechanism. It scales with your identity system, requires no pre-created resources, and covers every model and API operation. Application inference profiles work well when a small, stable set of business units needs invoice-grade billing separation without changes to identity design. Use projects for bedrock-mantle workloads that use the Responses API or Chat Completions API. CUR tells you who spent. Invocation logs tell you what happened. Amazon Bedrock supports model invocation logging of request data, response data, and metadata to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), or both. Use Amazon CloudWatch for fast operational queries and S3 plus Amazon Athena for long-term business intelligence (BI) access. Treat logging as infrastructure, not a manual toggle: provision the log group or bucket through code, define retention and encryption policies, and validate delivery during environment setup. If logging exists only in development or only in one Region, your cost program becomes fragmentary the moment usage grows. Logging also closes the latency gap: CUR attribution lags roughly 24 hours, but CloudWatch plus OpenTelemetry can power near-real-time dashboards showing per-developer spend within minutes ( Analyzing Claude Code usage with CloudWatch and OpenTelemetry demonstrates this end to end). Raw logs answer identity-level questions. To answer workload-level questions (which feature, workflow, or tenant generated the tokens), stamp request metadata on every call. Amazon Bedrock captures this metadata in the invocation logs for later analysis: The following example uses Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock through the US cross-Region inference profile. For the full list of models, see Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock . For availability by Region, see Model support by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock . Amazon Bedrock doesn’t enforce request metadata, and teams drift into inconsistent schemas quickly when every application does its own thing.

item.title: I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could
item.abstract: Gadgets AI Tech I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could We have Muse Charm at home. by Sean Hollister Oct 31, 2026, 4:05 PM UTC Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge Gadgets AI Tech I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could We have Muse Charm at home. by Sean Hollister Oct 31, 2026, 4:05 PM UTC Part Of Today I’m toying with see all updates Sean Hollister is a senior editor and founding member of The Verge who covers gadgets, games, and toys. He spent 15 years editing the likes of CNET, Gizmodo, and Engadget. Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta made AI look so stinking cute by giving it a squishy little face — and this holiday season, he wants to sell you a Muse Charm so you can carry your jolly AI helper around like a Tamagotchi. But I won’t be buying one, because we have Muse Charm at home . It cost just $50, and I’ve decided the learning experience was worth it. My version doesn’t sport cameras or a 5G cellular radio , but it really talks to Muse and has cute avatars, too! It doubles as a pocket watch and a remote camera viewfinder, and it can (theoretically) control my smart home. Or at least it can if you inject a lot of extra vibe code. Weeks ago, I paid $50 to get a 1.75-inch touchscreen computer pendant drop-shipped from China — specifically the Waveshare ESP32-S3 1.75C . Not only does the push-to-talk AI devkit look a lot like the Muse Charm, but it’s officially sanctioned by Meta. It’s one of the company’s first suggestions if you want to build a “Muse Gadget,” a device that uses Meta’s open-source code and tokens to directly connect to its Muse AI cloud. When the silver metal pocket watch arrived, it felt pretty useless to start. Setup was easy enough — I just plugged it into my PC and pointed Claude at Meta’s GitHub, then paired it to the Muse phone app. But even after I put Meta’s keys on the device, Muse originally thought I was sending it audio clips to transcribe rather than commands. After I cleared that up, Muse’s responses were still slow, and it didn’t answer me out loud. It was hard to tell what it was saying since it only showed a few words onscreen at a time, with no place to read full messages unless I whipped out my phone with its own Muse app. Meta’s build also only came with a single Jolly avatar that mostly just sat there and looked cute, and it wouldn’t automatically discover smart home gadgets like Amazon Echo or Google Home devices do. (This gadget really didn’t do anything useful after my initial install.) And though Meta AI software engineers Anant Narayanan and Jeremy Payne include a neat sample app showing how Muse Gadgets can stream video from your phone camera, the lack of a remote shutter button made it not so useful for taking photos. Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge But a few sessions of Claude Code filled in almost all those holes. All I had to do was plug the Waveshare back into my PC, then ask Claude to reprogram each thing I wanted. When I complained to Claude that I couldn’t properly read or hear Muse’s replies to my asks, issues that others have mentioned as well , Claude built a conversation history page so I can swipe right to read what it said, and I plugged in a British AI voice from ElevenLabs that speaks its answers out loud. (The voice was the least soul-sucking of the ones in ElevenLabs’ free tier, my wife and I agree, even if it doesn’t match the Muse avatars’ cuddly vibe at all.) Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge Thanks to Claude, I can now press a button to make my phone take a picture from across the room with a high-quality live preview, and my phone’s front-facing camera no longer displays upside down. Claude made fairly short work of adding a low-quality camera preview over Bluetooth, too, so I don’t need to be on home Wi-Fi to get photos from creative angles. When I hit this button on my new remote viewfinder… Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge …my phone takes a photo. Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge I asked Claude to make a whole batch of different avatars like the ones Meta showed off during Meta Connect, and to add a Tamagotchi-like minigame where they need food, play, sleep, and a bath. When the game seemed too simple to capture any attention, I had it add four different levels of hunger, boredom, and dirt. I decided treats should make a crunchy mess and get avatars dirtier when they eat them, and that too much play should tire out a pet. My wish was Claude’s command. When I noticed I was accidentally letting go of the push-to-talk button too soon and making Muse choke on almost-empty audio, vibe coding fixed it minutes later by sending only audio over one second in length. The only obvious lag I’m seeing now is from Meta’s own servers — sometimes they’re responsive, sometimes they lag quite a bit. Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge It was so easy to let Claude reprogram the pendant that I asked it to build a few features specifically for this video in this story, including a working pocket watch face with three hands that actually tells the time. (That took it 15 minutes; now, when I say the hardware looks like a pocket watch, you can see what I mean!) It even found, downloaded, trimmed, and loaded video clips of Zuck introducing the Muse Charm and installed a video player so I could play those clips on the Waveshare. I want you to understand I have no coding experience, and so I have no idea if any of this code is good. It might be fatally flawed. Nor do I trust Meta or its Muse agent with my email or my home network, particularly after hearing how it leaked one reviewer’s home address . (I put it on guest Wi-Fi from the get-go as a precaution.) That means I don’t really know how useful a Muse Charm may or may not be for those who do know how to code and are willing to take a bigger leap of faith. But after nearly dropping a bulky little silver pendant a couple of times, one with no more Muse functionality than my phone (and quite a bit less without additional code), I’m thinking Muse itself isn’t the reason to buy a dedicated compute pocket watch. The reason to have a dedicated piece of hardware is to do things you can’t do on the phone that’s already in your pocket, like coding the entire gadget to do whatever you want. Which makes me wonder: Will the actual Muse Charm be this freely programmable, or would the kind of people who’d buy one be better off with a development kit? I guess we’ll see when it ships. item.abstract: 百度 APP 釋出四大 AI 升級，搜尋已實現遞迴自我進化 聽雨 2026-10-30 16:50:44 來源： 量子位 10 月 30 日，百度 APP 在北京舉辦產品升級溝通會。百度搜索實現遞迴自我進化，並全新升級搜尋 AI API，活動期間最低價僅需 4.9 元/千次，低於 DeepSeek 搜尋 API。同時圍繞搜尋框、AI 鏡頭、GUI 視覺化、AI 互動應用等方向推出重大升級，給使用者帶來更智慧、更聰明、更好玩的體驗。 搜尋正在從「一次提問、一次回答」走向「一項任務、一份交付」。複雜問題可以交給搜尋做多步查詢與整理，直接返回核實彙總後的結論，高頻事務可以直接交付結果，把「查詢—跳轉—操作」壓縮成最短路徑；需要長期關注的事項，則在使用者確認後持續跟蹤，發現變化主動提醒。 目前這一能力已覆蓋 170 餘種工具場景。家長在搜尋升學資訊時，搜尋會結合此前記錄的孩子成績、家庭住址和寄宿偏好，把通勤、學費、招生政策放到一起比較，給出更具體的擇校建議；而使用者規劃春節三亞行程時，搜尋不僅生成完整的五天行程和預算，還會在酒店降價時主動提醒，五晚行程省下 2100 元。 在 AI 鏡頭方面，百度針對傳統拍照識物「看不全、說不清、問不深」的三大斷點，讓鏡頭從「定格」走向「流動」。升級後的鏡頭支援多目標同步識別與動態追蹤，畫面裡的多種植物、多件樂器可以一次認全，跳動的猴子、遊動的魚群，識別標籤都能穩穩跟隨，使用者不再需要費力描述目標，點一下、圈一下就能精準提問，拍照之後還可無縫切入即時對話，順著好奇心一層層追問，從「知其然」走向「知其所以然」。同時，AI 鏡頭支援東北話、四川話、粵語、長沙話等 9 種方言即時對話，讓「用鏡頭與世界對話」照進現實。 在 GUI 方面，搜尋頁的 GUI 場景覆蓋提升 5 倍，接入政務、民生、央行等超 50 億權威資源資料，覆蓋 20 多個行業，依託 AI 智慧視覺化與專業圖表模板，讓複雜資料「看得見、能比較、可互動」，並開放生態，權威專業資料機構、夥伴均可加入。 在 AI 互動應用方面，百度 APP 釋出 AI 互動劇與 AI 互動應用，使用者從「刷著看」變成「上手玩」，可以在互動劇中選擇劇情走向，也可以在互動應用中親手操作、獲得反饋，內容形態從單向消費走向參與共創。同步啟動的「百度 AI 未來創作聯賽」，以百萬現金激勵和億級流量扶持，向互動內容創作者丟擲橄欖枝。 值得注意的是，此次百度還全新升級了搜尋 AI API，限時最低價為每千次查詢 4.9 元，低於 DeepSeek 的搜尋 API 價格。 高性價比和好效果得益於其 AI 原生四層架構：內容層匯聚全球 80 餘種語言、千億級優質索引，資料可信率提升超過50%；引擎層通過線上反饋閉環實現多 Agent 協同自進化，百度搜索把每一次真實檢索與使用者反饋沉澱為訓練訊號，經「檢索—反饋—再訓練」閉環持續迴流，驅動模型遞迴式自我進化，在無需人工干預的情況下不斷迭代升級，整體迭代效率提升 80% 以上；架構層支援高併發低時延，具備優質企業級服務保障能力；應用層支援 API、MCP、Skill 全方案接入，文心助手接入後效果提升 20%。 百度 APP 以「搜得準、答得好、交付得了」重新定義 AI 應用競爭維度，給使用者帶來更智慧、更聰明、更好玩的體驗。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 聽雨 奧特曼和Dario同臺唱rap！Genspark新影片Agent上線，零基礎也能拍短劇 2026-10-29 KV Cache被壓成常數！OCR開源新王：頁數沒上限，快取砍96% 2026-10-27 國產AI 3D大模型Hi3D來了！開源可商用，PK幹掉GPT-6 2026-10-27 VAST開源即時世界模型EdenLive！單消費級顯示卡、720P超24FPS 2026-10-18

item.title: Tell HN: Scribd Breached
item.abstract:
Not seeing anything posted about this anywhere, received on Monday, 26th of Oct 2026: Subject: Notice of Security Incident This notice is being sent on behalf of Scribd, Inc., the parent company of Scribd, Slideshare, Everand, and Fable, by Epiq, Scribd Inc.’s notification partner. Hello, We are writing to let you know that Scribd, Inc. recently experienced a security incident that may have affected your data. We detected that an unauthorized third party may have gained access to certain user data in one of our systems. After investigating this activity, we found that the third party may have accessed your email address and the following of your information: last 4 digits of your credit card and country, credit card issuer, credit card expiry date, payment history (not including credit card details). We have no evidence that this data has been misused, but we are notifying you out of an abundance of caution so that you can take steps to protect your information. Watch for phishing We encourage you to stay vigilant for phishing attempts by bad actors pretending to be Scribd, Inc. or Scribd, Slideshare, Everand or Fable. Remember that Scribd, Inc. will never ask you for your username and password or other sensitive information via email or text. If you did receive a message like that:       Don't click on any links in it. Instead type scribd.com, slideshare.net, everand.com, or fable.co directly into your browser.
    Call us at: +1-877-361-9887. Hours of operation are Monday-Friday, 11:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m., Central European Time.
    Report it through Scribd, Inc.'s Help Center.
  
For more information We regret that this incident occurred and any concern it may cause you. If you have additional questions, contact the dedicated call center at +1-877-361-9887. Hours of operation are Monday-Friday, 11:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Central European Time. The National Cyber Security Center has helpful guidance on how to recognize and avoid phishing scams here. What Scribd, Inc. is doing       We have secured the affected system and ended the unauthorized access.
    We have notified law enforcement as well as the relevant data protection authorities.
    We are working with an expert third party cybersecurity firm to strengthen our access controls and monitoring.
  
We value the trust you place in us with your information, and don’t take that lightly. We are deeply sorry this happened and will keep you updated if anything further changes. Scribd, Inc.
